# Linux: build or install the BPM improvements branch

Run as your normal user from the `bpm-improvements` checkout:

```sh
./install-linux.sh
```

The installer asks whether to **build** (`b`) or **install with a starter**
(`i`). For non-interactive use, select a mode explicitly:

```sh
./install-linux.sh --mode build
./install-linux.sh --mode install
```

The shell entry point delegates to `tools/install-linux.py`. You can also run
that Python script directly. Both entry points use the adjacent checkout,
regardless of the directory from which you invoke them.

- **Build:** compiles Mixxx and prints a complete start command with resource
  and settings paths. It does not install files or create shortcuts.
- **Install:** additionally runs `cmake --install` into a user-local prefix,
  creates `~/.local/bin/mixxx-bpm-improvements`, and adds **Mixxx (BPM
  Improvements)** to the desktop application menu. The starter uses absolute
  paths and forwards all arguments to Mixxx.

This branch uses the native Queen Mary and SoundTouch analyzers. No Beat This!,
PyTorch, ONNX, virtual environment, inference worker or checkpoint is installed.
Python 3.8+ runs the installer only. New profiles use the branch's native Auto
tempo mode; the installer never rewrites existing profile settings.

## Native prerequisites

```sh
./install-linux.sh --print-deps
```

Provide CMake >= 3.22, a C++20 compiler, pkg-config, Make or Ninja, and Mixxx's
native development libraries. The current Debian/Ubuntu dependency list is in
`tools/debian_buildenv.sh` and `packaging/debian/control.in`; it includes Qt6
private headers, Multimedia, SVG, OpenGL, qtkeychain, SQLite and the required
audio, codec, USB and MIDI libraries. For a fresh Qt6 installation, also check
the QtQml, QtQml.Models and QtQuick runtime modules.

The repository provides `tools/debian_buildenv.sh setup` for Debian/Ubuntu,
`tools/rpm_buildenv.sh setup` for Fedora and `tools/archlinux_buildenv.sh setup`
for Arch. Those dependency setup scripts may use administrator privileges.
The installer itself never invokes `sudo` or a system package manager. Missing
dependencies stop CMake configuration before compilation.

New build directories use Release and disable tests/benchmarks. Existing caches
retain their build type and test options. Additional CMake arguments are accepted
as `--cmake-arg=-DNAME=VALUE`. For development, for example:

```sh
./install-linux.sh --mode build --jobs 4 \
  --cmake-arg=-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug --cmake-arg=-DOPTIMIZE=off \
  --cmake-arg=-DBUILD_TESTING=ON
```

Use separate build directories for different source trees or toolchains. The
installer rejects a cache from a different source directory. It fixes installation
destinations to relative `bin`, `share`, `lib` and `share/doc/mixxx` directories
under the selected prefix. It does not install system udev rules; real controllers
may require permissions configured separately by an administrator.

## Locations and profiles

| Item | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Installation prefix | `~/.local/opt/mixxx-bpm-improvements` |
| Standalone-managed sources | `~/.local/share/mixxx-bpm-improvements/source` |
| Build directory | `~/.cache/mixxx-bpm-improvements/build` |
| Dedicated settings and library database | `~/.config/mixxx-bpm-improvements` |
| Command, install mode only | `~/.local/bin/mixxx-bpm-improvements` |
| Desktop entry, install mode only | `~/.local/share/applications/org.mixxx.Mixxx.BpmImprovements.desktop` |

`XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` override their usual
defaults. These locations are separate from the old Beat This! installer and
from `~/.mixxx`. Existing libraries and settings are not migrated automatically.
Close Mixxx using the selected profile before installing or updating.

```sh
./install-linux.sh --mode build \
  --build-dir "$HOME/build/mixxx-bpm" --jobs 4

./install-linux.sh --mode install \
  --prefix "$HOME/Applications/Mixxx BPM" \
  --profile "$HOME/.config/mixxx-bpm-improvements"
```

`--skip-build` reuses an existing executable only when its CMake cache matches
the selected sources. In install mode the cached prefix and relative installation
layout must also match; otherwise rerun without `--skip-build`. This option does
not prove that an executable contains later source edits. Rebuild after changing
C++ sources or switching revisions.

The script refuses to replace unrelated starter files or links. To remove the
installation, remove its prefix, command link and desktop entry. Build directories
and managed sources can be removed separately; keep the profile to retain its data.

## Standalone use and updates

The Python helper can also be downloaded by itself. Review it before running:

```sh
curl -fLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabba43/mixxx/bpm-improvements/tools/install-linux.py
python3 install-linux.py --mode build
```

If no adjacent sources are found, it clones `https://github.com/gabba43/mixxx.git`
at `bpm-improvements` into the managed source directory. `--repository` and `--ref`
can select another repository/ref containing these native BPM improvements.
`--source-dir /path/to/mixxx` selects existing sources or a new clone destination.
Source archives are supported without Git.

Managed sources update with `git pull --ff-only --no-rebase`. Local tracked edits,
divergence, a mismatched branch/origin or a failed update stop the build without
resetting or stashing anything. A tag stays pinned. Developer checkouts outside
the managed path are used unchanged unless you explicitly pass `--update`.
`--no-update` builds the existing revision; `--skip-build` also skips updates and
cannot be combined with `--update`. The source directory, branch and full commit
are printed before building.

## Compile memory budget

The interactive budget choices are 25%, 50% or 75% of RAM. Non-interactive runs
default to 50%; `--ram-percent 25` selects a value explicitly. The budget accounts
for lower cgroup-v2 limits and is capped at 80% of currently available memory.
Parallelism is estimated at 1.5 GiB per job and capped by CPU count and `--jobs`.

Where a user `systemd-run` memory scope is available, compilation and linking run
with `MemoryMax` equal to that budget and `MemorySwapMax=0`. Otherwise the script
reports that it only adjusts parallelism and cannot enforce a hard RAM limit.
`--skip-build` skips the budget prompt. Allow several GB of disk space and enough
time for a first native build.

## Validation

Installer regression tests:

```sh
python3 tools/test_install_linux.py
```

For a build configured with `BUILD_TESTING=ON`, run `ctest --test-dir <build-dir>
--parallel 4 --output-on-failure`. CTest isolates tests in separate processes;
running the entire `mixxx-test` suite in one process exposes existing shared-state
conflicts. Without a physical display, set `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` and
`QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software`. These checks do not replace a manual test with real
audio and controller hardware.
